gloss: to tempt; to seduce; to lure

definitions.gloss: to tempt; to lure; to entice
definitions.explanation: To attract or entice someone toward something, often something they should resist. The temptation may involve food, money, pleasure, or other desires.
To attract someone romantically or sexually, often with the implication of leading them away from proper behavior.

examples.japanese: ケーキに{誘惑|ゆうわく}された。
examples.english: I was tempted by the cake.

examples.japanese: {甘|あま}い{言葉|ことば}で{誘惑|ゆうわく}してくる。
examples.english: They try to lure you with sweet words.

examples.japanese: ダイエット{中|ちゅう}なのに、{目|め}の{前|まえ}のスイーツに{誘惑|ゆうわく}されて{食|た}べてしまった。
examples.english: Even though I was on a diet, I was tempted by the sweets in front of me and ended up eating them.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}を{誘惑|ゆうわく}しようとした。
{映画|えいが}の{中|なか}で{悪魔|あくま}が{主人公|しゅじんこう}を{誘惑|ゆうわく}する{場面|ばめん}が{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった。
examples.english: The scene in the movie where the devil tempts the protagonist was memorable.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{巧|たく}みな{話術|わじゅつ}で{相手|あいて}を{誘惑|ゆうわく}し、{大金|たいきん}を{騙|だま}し{取|と}った。
examples.english: He seduced his target with skillful rhetoric and swindled a large sum of money.

notes:
A compound of {誘|ゆう} (to invite; to lead) and {惑|わく} (to be confused; to go astray). The noun form {誘惑|ゆうわく} is also very common, used in phrases like {誘惑|ゆうわく}に{負|ま}ける (to give in to temptation).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {誘惑|ゆうわく}に{負|ま}ける: to give in to temptation
- {誘惑|ゆうわく}に{勝|か}つ: to resist temptation
- {誘惑|ゆうわく}に{抗|あらが}う: to fight against temptation
- {誘惑|ゆうわく}に{駆|か}られる: to be driven by temptation
- {甘|あま}い{誘惑|ゆうわく}: sweet temptation

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {誘|さそ}う: to invite; to lure — more neutral; covers friendly invitations as well as enticement
- {惑|まど}わす: to lead astray; to bewitch — emphasizes confusion and deception
- {口説|くど}く: to woo; to come on to — specifically romantic/sexual persuasion, more direct
